newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 43-50 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 43-50 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 43 to 50 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 30 bcf to 70 bcf for the week ended October 25. The four-week average is 68 bcf.
"I don't expect a big number. There was some incremental load last week that took up some of the flow (of injections)," said one Houston-based trader.
Last week, AGA showed overall storage gained 57 bcf, in line with expectations. Stocks were still 256 bcf, or nine percent, below the same year-ago period.
Eastern stocks rose to 93 percent of capacity last week, about even with last year. Most expected eastern builds to slow as storage nears capacity.
Producing region inventories in last report continued to seriously lag 1995 levels at just 72 percent full. Stocks in the region last year were at 88 percent of capacity.

Last year at this time, total inventories gained 34 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to 1995 to about 243 bcf. For the same week in 1995, eastern storage rose by 21 bcf, while producing stocks were up 12 bcf.
